correctness.rationale: In H=ell²(N), take V_j=C and Lambda_j=Gamma_j: f↦f_j. Both are g-Parseval and globally alternate dual, since ∑ Lambda_j*Gamma_j=I. Each one-dimensional local pair phi_j=1/j, psi_j=j is an exact alternate dual frame for C, satisfying reconstruction phi_j·psi_j=1, though their optimal local frame bounds j^{-2} and j² are not uniform. The induced vectors Lambda_j*phi_j=e_j/j lack a uniform lower bound because testing f=e_N gives coefficient energy N^{-2}; Gamma_j*psi_j=j e_j lack an upper Bessel bound because testing e_N gives N². Moreover f=(1/j)_j is in ell² but has analysis coefficients (1)_j against (j e_j), not in ell². Thus printed Corollary 6.2’s (i) holds and (ii), which asserts alternate dual *frames*, is false. The block local reconstruction Q=I is bounded and cannot cure lack of global Bessel bounds. If both local families share global finite upper frame bounds, bounded induced analysis maps and the mixed reconstruction identity reestablish the equivalence. In the scalar diagonal model both families (a_j e_j),(a_j^{-1}e_j) are frames iff 0<inf a_j<=sup a_j<infinity; this exact all-N basis argument, not finite truncation, establishes necessity.
residual_risks: This disproves the printed Corollary 6.2 under literal hypotheses; a tacit inherited common-bound condition would yield a different valid assertion.

value.rationale: An exact published duality characterization can fail at the fundamental stability requirement of frames, not merely at a weak constant. The e_j/j and j e_j witness isolates the missing local-to-global uniformity with bounded block reconstruction Q=I; the repair restores a functioning theorem. The sharp diagonal seminormalization boundary quantifies precisely when reciprocal local duals remain a global dual pair. This is a motivated flaw in generalized frame reconstruction, despite elementary ingredients.
residual_risks: The construction is simple and related locality defects are known in frame literature; value rests on the specific incorrect printed claim and precise boundary, not generic novelty of rescaling.
